result:
I would make changing your mind feel like relief instead of defeat.

Right now, the human brain processes a challenge to a deeply held belief almost the same way it processes a physical threat. Being wrong feels like losing status, losing safety, or losing yourself. Because of that single wiring quirk, people defend terrible ideas, prolong wars, ignore catastrophic problems, and fracture the people they love—all to avoid a flinch of the ego.

If I could change one thing, I would decouple who people are from what they currently think. Imagine if realizing *“I had that completely wrong”* felt the way it feels to set down a heavy bag you didn't notice you were carrying, or to finally find the missing piece of a puzzle.

It wouldn't magically erase scarcity, disease, or genuine conflicts of interest. The world would still be hard. But humanity would suddenly be able to actually face its problems, instead of spending most of its energy pretending it never made a mistake in the first place.
